#1524. Doubts had been gathering about Roberto De Zerbi but not now, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, as Crystal Palace's ludicrous acts of self-sabotage prove costly in 2-0 defeat

By RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:56 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 10:07 EDT, 1 November 2026

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham have won three games in succession. If that proves Roberto De Zerbi’s prowess over at least two of his predecessors, then he will presumably reserve some thanks to the assistance of Crystal Palace.

On a night when Palace crossed to the north of London, with their manager in grave danger of the sack, they contrived to commit an utterly ludicrous act of self-sabotage in two phases.

The first defined the match, with Jean-Philippe Mateta dismissed after only 13 minutes for a challenge that was as brainless as it was dangerous.

From there, Pierre Sage’s side quickly conceded from a set-piece with the sort of defending that explained why Palace have shipped more goals than any other team in the top flight. That no further damage was inflicted until Jan Paul van Hecke’s second-half header was less reflective of the game than the tally showing 34 Tottenham shots to Palace’s two.

Given Sage’s tenuous grip on his job, and the thunderous face in the crowd of his chairman, Steve Parish, that might prove to be the final straw. If it is, Mateta should at least have the decency to drive him to the airport.

Sage said: ‘I am responsible. I have to find solutions. They have to trust in me because I will give my life for it. If I have one hour or 10 years, I will try my best.’

Archie Gray opened the scoring for Tottenham after 25 minutes to settle the nerves

Jan Paul van Hecke slid in to make it 2-0 and all but wrap the game up for the home team

In the recent past, such doubts were gathering around De Zerbi, but not now, and especially with a favourable run of fixtures on the horizon. Having belatedly entered the top half of the table, his side are finally aligning results with performances, even if this fourth game in an unbeaten stretch was aided so much by the opposition.

There remains an issue with chance conversion – both Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush were underwhelming here, with the slight mitigation that Palace spent the better part of 75 minutes camped on the edge of their own area. Marmoush, who started at No 10 after earlier games on the left and up front, appears no closer to revealing his best position.

De Zerbi’s solution was to direct traffic to the wings and it worked a treat. Mathys Tel, riding the isolated high of his performance against Chelsea, was again sharp. So too Mohammed Kudus. But the real gains for Tottenham in this purple patch have come from the central pairing of Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes.

They cost a fortune to acquire and have taken their sweet time to gel, but that partnership has developed to strong effect. On the ball, they are the tempo setters, and off it they have shaped the press that is key to De Zerbi’s system. They controlled this game.

‘Tonali was unbelievable,’ said De Zerbi. ‘We played with two players more - Tonali (counted) double.’

He added: ‘I am very happy with the performance. (But) if we want perfection we have to be more nasty. If I am No 9 or No 10 I want to score.’

The last sentence is very much the Tottenham riddle – an inability to finish what they start. But those frustrations are now coming from an upwardly mobile situation.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi is banishing the doubters as his team climb the table

Having belatedly entered the top half of the table, Spurs are finally aligning results with performances

For Sage, along with whatever consequences this result brings, the regret will come from knowing his side had looked decent out of the gate.

But the red card eradicated those traces of momentum. Initially, referee Michael Oliver felt a booking was sufficient for Mateta’s studs-up lunge into Micky van de Ven’s ankle, but the VAR suggested an upgrade. On review, Oliver agreed.

Sage’s reaction? He had a look of pure deflation. The tackle was bad enough but the need to make it was non-existent – Mateta was chasing a losing cause in Tottenham’s half against one of the quickest defenders in the league. Dismal.

Naturally, it shifted the game in Tottenham’s favour, if only to the effect of a one-goal lead by the break. As with Mateta’s dismissal, the Spurs breakthrough was avoidable for Palace, with Gray left unmarked at the far post before planting his head on Kudus’s high, looping corner.

The video analysis will do Sage no favours. Kudus’s delivery was excellent, that much is true, but five Tottenham men had gathered at the far post with only three markers – even factoring for the red card, the tracking of Gray was abysmal.

At half-time, De Zerbi substituted Gray, who was carrying a yellow card, and Spurs maintained momentum by creating openings for Tel, Matheus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Solanke.

Palace were being pummelled but survived until Van Hecke’s finish for 2-0. As with the Chelsea win, Fernandes stood out in its creation with an excellent cross, from which Van Hecke powered a header at Dean Henderson.

The initial save was good, but the ball returned to Van Hecke, who was sat on his backside and able to steer his second header past Henderson. Sage could use similar inspiration from the floor.

Recent form has been uneven. The last five league results were a 2-0 home win over Atalanta, a 1-1 draw at Cagliari and a 3-0 home defeat by Lazio. A 2-0 win at Lecce and the loss at Genoa complete the run. Two of those five games ended in defeat, and Juventus failed to score in both.

#1521. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE

Andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

So far, four of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season have played on this opening matchday and all four have won:

Atletico had more possession in the second half but Liverpool were much the better side after the break.

"We can achieve everything we want." 💪Dominik Szoboszlai full of belief after Liverpool's Champions League victory over Atletico Madrid 👀🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ebSvagW4yx

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ

First Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a new contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

We are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

Alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

What a save from Alisson! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PuajED3Rks

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

We are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

The two sides emerge from the tunnel to a cacophony of noise and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. The home fans boo the Champions League anthem and belt out “Liverpool! Liverpool!” over the top of it. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

Liverpool: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.Substitutes: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Tsimikas, Munoz, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Chambers, McConnell, Koumas, Danns.

Atletico Madrid: Oblak; Llorente, Pubill, Romero, Hancko; Simeone, Barrios, Koke, Baena; Alvarez, Lee.Substitutes: Musso, Vargaz, Mendoza, Cardoso, Lookman, David, Grimaldo, Hjulmand, Le Normand, Dominguez, Martinez, Castillo.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

#1520. Alajbegović’s first Serie A goal and Boga sink ten-man Napoli on Juventus’s birthday

Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium, with both goals arriving after a goalless first half. Luciano Spalletti's side now sit seventh, with Napoli eighth, ahead of a Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

The result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

Napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

Spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

Napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

Sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win important for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

Primo gol in carriera in Serie A, così. ✨ pic.twitter.com/TTGoL4MMyR

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 1, 2026

It was a second straight league win over Napoli for Juventus, who beat them 3-0 on 25 January 2026. Napoli’s defeat ended a run that included a 4-1 win over Monza. They now face FC Porto away in the Champions League on Wednesday 4 November.

Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League League Phase on Thursday 5 November, with kick-off at 21:00 CET.

He’s not the first inductee and he won’t be the last, with several of the Rossoneri’s legends not yet part of the members.

With 30 candidates named, there is no shortage of choice and Paolo Maldini’s place within the vote will be welcomed. Of course, he’s not alone, though, with several other notable names joining him, as can be seen below.

Voting for the new edition of the Hall of Fame is now open! Presented by @emirates✈️

We all know which two must be there, it’s only that third player that should be the topic (subject) of a/the debate but, whoever ends up in the third place in this peculiar voting, he’ll be way below #3 and #6, percentage-wise…

Wait, what? AC Milan fans actually have to VOTE for Paolo Maldini to enter the club’s Hall of Fame? Is this some kind of joke? How is he not already there?

This is beyond ridiculous. It’s downright insulting to the history and identity of AC Milan.

Perhaps the American ownership should take a moment to actually learn the history of the club they’re running. Here’s a little history lesson: the numbers #6 and #3 were RETIRED in honour of Franco Baresi and Paolo Maldini. Ring any bells?

These two aren’t just Hall of Fame candidates. They ARE AC Milan’s history, legacy and identity. There should never even be a discussion about their inclusion, let alone a public vote.

You don’t ask fans to vote on whether legends like Maldini and Baresi deserve to belong in Milan’s history. They’re the reason that history is worth celebrating in the first place.

Show some respect. This is AC Milan, not a marketing campaign.

#1518. Patrick Battiston, the horrible fright

The scene is undoubtedly part of the legend of French football. The name of Harald Schumacher is likely to send a shiver down the spine of all the supporters of the Blues who experienced the famous semi-final of the 1982 World Cup between France and West Germany, where the attack on Patrick Battiston by the German goalkeeper took place.

Unfortunately, and very sadly, this episode experienced a disastrous remake during a Spanish D2 match where Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife striker, lost his life following violent contact with Jesus Owono, the Andorra goalkeeper, very far from his goal. In both cases, it is a goalkeeper who comes out in a reckless manner and hits the opposing attacker with his hip. Jesus de Miguel was hit in the chest, which caused a cardio-respiratory arrest. Battiston had been hit in the head.

Seeing him lying on the ground, lifeless, the Blues at the time feared for the life of their teammate. Meanwhile, Harald Schumacher remained on the sidelines, without showing the slightest consideration for his opponent, preparing to shoot from six meters: the referee did not even call a foul on this action!

Immediately, medical staff came to help Patrick Battiston. The Blues defender was then unconscious, the doctor will even have difficulty finding his pulse. He will end up being evacuated on a stretcher, with his captain Michel Platini holding his hand, his face defeated. Highly worried.

Taken to hospital, Patrick Battiston will have to remain under observation all night. The result, ultimately, was three broken teeth, head trauma and a fracture of the cervical vertebrae. A lesser evil, somewhere, especially since we now know that the worst was possible.

A few years later, Harald Schumacher made his mea culpa. “I regret everything that happened after the clash with Battiston. I already apologized for not checking on him when he was knocked out. But then I told myself that if I got closer things could get out of hand, explains the German goalkeeper. After the match, a journalist intercepted me to inform me that Battiston had lost two teeth. I was relieved because I was afraid it would be much more serious. »

#1517. Falkirk 2-0 Celtic: Pressure is mounting on Martin O'Neill as Scottish giants suffer a sixth defeat in 10 matches - as hosts celebrate their first win over Bhoys since 2007

Published: 10:11 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 10:55 EDT, 1 November 2026

Celtic paid the price for a sloppy start and a superb display from former goalkeeper Scott Bain as they fell to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk.

Ethan Ross netted in the third minute after a mistake by Cameron Carter-Vickers and Scott Tanser put Falkirk two ahead in the 38th minute.

Bain made ten saves as Martin O’Neill’s side endured an afternoon of frustration and suffered a sixth defeat in ten matches.

The champions remain four points clear at the top of the William Hill Premiership but have now played a game more than second-placed Rangers.

Falkirk moved up to fourth in the table after their fourth consecutive victory and their first over Celtic since 2007.

Carter-Vickers returned to the starting line-up after injury, while Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was handed his first start in two months. Winger Haissem Hassan was recalled.

Kasper Hogh might have fancied himself to end his barren run on Falkirk’s synthetic pitch given most of his career goals have come on artificial surfaces, but the former Bodo/Glimt striker was dropped as Camilo Duran led the line.

Martin O'Neill looks on in dismay as Celtic suffer in Falkirk

The Danish striker came on for the final 25 minutes but was barely involved as he went 14 games without a goal.

Falkirk got an early lift after the Celtic central defence failed to deal with a long ball.

The hosts worked the ball out to Ryan Strain, whose cross was knocked into the path of Ross by Carter-Vickers. The wide player lapped up the chance.

The goal came at a cost as Strain injured himself while crossing. Jack McMillan was a natural replacement at right-back.

Both sides made opportunities in the first half.

Celtic winger Haissem Hassan is in the thick of it during a scuffle at the Falkirk Stadium

Owen Eames hails goalscorer Scott Tanser after he scored Falkirk's second

On-loan Derby winger Owen Eames was a hive of creativity on Falkirk’s left wing and helped set up two half chances for Jacob Murrell, who could not make the most of them.

The 19-year-old wide player set up the second goal as left-back Tanser ran on to his infield pass before slotting past Sam Johnstone.

Duran hit a post after getting in behind and Celtic were kept out by a string of excellent first-half stops from Bain, who denied the Colombian three times and also foiled Hassan with a diving save.

Falkirk were almost out of sight early in the second half when Murrell bundled the ball over the line after Celtic failed to deal with a long throw, but the ball had hit the American’s hand when it bounced off a post before going in off the striker’s waist and the goal was disallowed by VAR.

O’Neill had brought on James Forrest for Callum Osmand at half-time and the winger forced Bain’s first save of the half before Callum McGregor, Kieran Tierney and Hassan missed the target from inside the box.

O’Neill turned to Hogh and Benjamin Nygren as Duran and Oxlade-Chamberlain made way.

Celtic captain Callum McGregor looks frustrated during their loss to Falkirk

But Bain quickly pulled off a brilliant double save from Forrest and Nygren to spark chants of ‘Scotland’s number one’.

The former Celtic goalkeeper soon denied Forrest again before Nygren was thwarted by a diving block from Finn Yeats.

It grew increasingly clear that Celtic were never going to score as Liam Scales headed over and Bain saved long-range efforts from Nygren and Mika Baur.

#1516. Amorim discusses Milan’s consistency, identity and disappointments so far: “We can beat anyone”

Ahead of Thursday’s Europa League game against Ferencvaros, AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim spoke to the media.

Tomorrow, Milan will be forced to bounce back in Europe with three points. It’s been an up-and-down campaign for them so far, losing to Benfica and Bournemouth, but they grabbed a win against RB Salzburg.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A top-eight place is not out of the question, but they will have to be perfect for all of their remaining games in the Europa League league phase. In short, it will not be easy, but it’s not impossible.

Tomorrow, the Portuguese is expected to rotate heavily, offering some of his senior players a chance to rest after a very busy October. For example, Strahinja Pavlovic didn’t train today and isn’t expected to start, either.

Speaking alongside Koni De Winter, Amorim addressed the quality of his opponents, rotations and his assessments of the season so far, as MilanNews relays.

The Derby was a good one, but now it’s behind them. Milan needs consistency…

“This is the objective. The Inter game is over and we need to focus on the Europa League. We were very consistent during the derby, but there were games where we weren’t. This is the big step forward we need to take.

“Rotation doesn’t matter, nor the players we field: we need to be a great team. We need to win tomorrow, because it’s crucial to our goal of going all the way in this competition.”

“First of all, the most important match is the next one. We have to be very careful with some players. We have this busy schedule behind us and we can’t afford to lose many players for the next matches, because sometimes, when you don’t want to rotate your squad, you end up with an injury that keeps you out for a month or a month and a half.

“This is the most important match; we’re only thinking about it, but we’ll have to rotate a bit, and all the players are ready to handle the impact of the demands of the game. We have the desire to win the match.

“We’ll be facing a great opponent who has nine points in this competition, a team that hasn’t lost a single game in the league, but our players are ready, and we have a duty to win.”

Why this difference between Serie A and the Europa League?

“But if you look at the games against Benfica, I think we didn’t play our best, despite having more possession. We had some problems with the few chances we gave the opponent, and we conceded goals.

“Then we won a great game in Salzburg and then in Bournemouth. We had a red card, two penalties, and it was our fault. Maignan’s situation didn’t help us fight for the game, and sometimes these dynamics happen at certain times.

“I think we’re not doing very well in Serie A; obviously, we won the last one, but looking at the team and the games, I think we should have more points. So I’m not satisfied in the Europa League, I’m not satisfied in Serie A.

“I think we can do better, but that’s how it goes sometimes. Every game has its own story. But I think we can do better tomorrow and win.”

“They’re a team that’s used to winning, no matter the context. It gives you full confidence in every game. They’re comfortable. They’re doing very well in the league. They play a 4-2-3-1 formation and have a strong identity.

“In midfield, Nagy is very good at building play. They’re comfortable; they come to San Siro with nothing to lose. The responsibility at San Siro is ours: we have to play well and stay focused.

“I told the players that against Inter we did well because we remained humble and attentive to detail: against Ferencvaros, we’ll have to do the same because they’re a very strong team.”

After the Europa League draw, Antonio Cassano said that Milan and Juventus cannot take victory against Ferencvaros for granted…

“Without a doubt. We’re capable of winning every match and losing every match. It depends on our approach, regardless of the opponent. Everyone knows everyone; every player has the tools to understand, and the coaches have the tools to prepare everything as best as possible.

“We can win and lose against anyone; it’s all up to us. And sometimes you also need a little bit of luck.”

Does your AC Milan already have a clear identity? Are we far off?

You often ask me when we’ll reach the top. We’ll never reach the top, even if we win every game. We always have to improve. We already have an identity: we want to dominate games, sometimes we manage to do it, sometimes we don’t.

“Sometimes we change the formation and the defensive phase and nobody even notices. Our identity is to be proactive: we still lack the ability to put opponents in the box to create more chances.

“But we’re playing better, we even manage certain moments better. But there’s still a lot of work to do, especially in the final 30 meters: I have to help my players do that.

On the excellent defensive phase against Inter:

“Inter are a thing of the past. We can show tomorrow that we can defend better. We defended, but with the ball. It allowed us to think better. Details are important: a meter is a meter. We were better than Bologna.

“We were very aggressive on the wings. Koni was exceptional, but if a cross comes in for Thuram, it’s very difficult to defend, so we were more aggressive without the ball to avoid crosses. We have to do the same tomorrow; they are used to winning games.

“When a team consistently wins, there must be a reason, and we have to be ready for tomorrow.”

“We have to give him credit; he’s working really well. He went through a period without playing and was a bit frustrated, but he’s always worked very well. I think he can play this role on the wing. We played with Moreira there once, but against Inter it was Diawara. Same role, different interpretation.

“During the break, against Padova, we tried him at left back: he showed important signs. He’s quick, he’s strong. He’s doing well, he has the potential to improve a lot. Against Inter, we knew how dangerous crosses could be, especially from Inter’s left flank.

“Dimarco didn’t play, but the tactical idea remained the same, and defending crosses with Koni and Pavlovic proved to be a good idea. They almost scored from a cross with Calhanoglu, but I think he’s doing really well.

“He has plenty of room for improvement, and who knows, maybe he’ll start tomorrow.”

“What I was saying about winning games, this is the team’s strength, our identity. I always put the team first, not the individual, even though we have excellent individual players. The Ferencvaros striker is very strong in space: he can play both as a winger and as a forward, and I think he’ll play as a striker against us.

“Nagy is an important player because he understands the game. He knows exactly when to drop back and when to stay high, and I really like that kind of player.

“Add to this the quality of the left-back with his right foot who can cut inside: all these little details define an identity that I really appreciate in this team, and we’ll have to be ready to process all this information to prepare and win the match.

“I repeat: we have three points in this competition and we absolutely must win tomorrow.”

It was the best second half of the entire championship, the one against Inter. I saw the attitude of a great team: authoritative, confident, without taking risks. Should we start again from the second half?

“I think it’s a good point. But you can’t separate the second half from the first; they’re connected. We took the lead in the first half, then we controlled the game that way in the second half. We improved our understanding of the game; we were complete in all areas.

“Maybe we were lacking in putting a few players behind Inter’s midfield: we had good possession, but we can do even better. It’s just one game, anyway. But thinking only about the derby is a small-team mentality: every game is important to us.

“Tomorrow I’ll understand my team better than the derby. I don’t care about the Inter game anymore. Was it nice to win? Yes. But I’m still angry about the Bologna game. Tomorrow we’ll have to be strong to win.”

The Derby showed a side of Cardinale emotional… When will we see her like this too?

“When we win the Scudetto or a major title, maybe I’ll be excited. Until then, it’s just another day. But I didn’t expect to feel this way during the match, and neither did Cardinale. He gave an important interview, saying he supports the coach.

“There was a wonderful feeling in the stadium; he enjoyed this moment and was emotional. He’s American, but when you spend time here, you become a little Italian. However, I won’t be excited until I win something. And when I do win something, I’ll already be thinking about the next Scudetto. I doubt you’ll see me emotional.”

#1515. McKennie ruled out of AZ trip with adductor fatigue as Alajbegović and Cabal return

Weston McKennie will miss Thursday's Europa League game at AZ Alkmaar with fatigue in his right adductor, though he has no muscle tear. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal are fit again, a relief for a badly stretched squad before a demanding trip.

Juventus will travel to AZ Alkmaar without Weston McKennie. The American has fatigue in his adductor and will sit out Thursday’s Europa League match. The news is not all bad. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal, who also came off in the 2-0 win over Napoli, have both been cleared.

McKennie lasted only the first half at the Allianz Stadium. Federico Gatti replaced him at the break. Luciano Spalletti had to send on an extra defender because McKennie felt a pull in his adductor. The coach also had few other players to choose from.

A short rest should be enough, because the injury is fatigue rather than a tear, Sky Sport Italia reported. He should be back for the league. The problem is in his right adductor. The medical staff will check him again before Thursday, ANSA said.

Alajbegović had both a goal and a scare against Napoli. He opened the scoring in the 70th minute and was replaced by Jérémie Boga two minutes later. Boga then added the second in the 87th. At 19 years and 41 days, the teenager has set a new mark: no non-Italian scorer in a Serie A meeting of these two clubs has been younger.

His knee knock has already cleared up. Cabal made way for Andrea Cambiaso after 83 minutes with cramp. That is put down to him not having started a game for some time. He will be available in Alkmaar.

Their return matters because the squad is badly stretched. Seven players are on the long-term injury list. Rugani, Zhegrova, Ekhator and Milik were left out of the UEFA squad. Losing McKennie, who can play several positions, leaves Spalletti with even fewer options for the trip to the Netherlands.

The match at AZ kicks off at 21:00 CET on 5 November. It is Matchday 4 of the league phase. Juventus have two wins and a draw so far.

AZ will be hard to break down at home. Their last home defeat in Europe was 4-1 to Aston Villa in the Conference League in October 2023.

Juventus arrive in good scoring form. They have nine goals in this season’s Europa League. Only Benfica, with ten, have scored more. That is Juventus’s best total after three games of a European campaign since 1999/2000.

⚪⚫ Kerim Alajbegović's first league goal for Juventus ✅#UEL | @juventusfc pic.twitter.com/GPcn8KJZga

— UEFA Europa League (@EuropaLeague) November 2, 2026

History against Dutch opposition also offers encouragement. Juventus are unbeaten in three previous Europa League games against Dutch clubs, with two wins and one draw. They scored seven goals and conceded one in those matches.

McKennie’s absence will shape the midfield in Alkmaar, but the focus will quickly shift to his recovery. His place for the next league game is in doubt. Juventus visit Fiorentina on Matchday 11, on Sunday 8 November 2026 at 20:45.

Juventus have tied academy forward Destiny Elimoghale to the club until 30 June 2029, on the day Giovanni Carnevali spoke to shareholders about the youth sector. The 2009-born striker has already been named in a European squad while injuries stretch the first team.

The club announced Elimoghale’s renewal on 3 November. That was the same day chief executive Giovanni Carnevali addressed shareholders at the Allianz Stadium. He called for a single project covering the first team, the Next Gen and the youth sector.

At Trento on the 11th matchday, he replaced Leone in the 70th minute of a 2-1 defeat. The match came in Serie C Group A. He was among Massimo Brambilla’s unused substitutes in the 1-1 home draw with Pro Vercelli on 2 November. That matchday 12 fixture was the Next Gen’s most recent game.

Carnevali said the club must bring its youth sector back to the level of recent years. He added that Juventus must keep trying to improve it. Securing a home-grown forward for the long term is consistent with that message.

Carnevali confirmed a change to the UEFA squad list as well, with Ekhator replacing Locatelli.

#1512. Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

#1511. Mikel Arteta's mission to conquer his Anfield demons: Why Arsenal boss must overcome psychological damage from his playing days and take the handbrake off as he plots first win at Liverpool, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 08:47 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 11:13 EDT, 1 November 2026

The word 'Anfield' still haunts Mikel Arteta.

It was there, 12 years ago, that the Spaniard suffered a chastening experience after losing 5-1 there as an Arsenal player in February 2014.

In a subsequent interview with Spanish newspaper Marca, Arteta used the term 'pajara' - a Spanish phrase com monly associated with cyclists who suddenly run out of energy - to describe a sensation mirroring mental paralysis. He had been caught up in an Anfield tornado.

'Suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around, the game is passing all over me and I cannot react,' Arteta reflected.

'Everyone is thinking, 'What is he doing?' I cannot react, emotionally, physical. I cannot cope, everything goes fast and I only had that feeling in my career once - and it was at Anfield.'

Such was the impact of that trauma that Arteta felt compelled to bring a slice of Anfield to Arsenal's London Colney base ahead of a league meeting in November 2021.

Mikel Arteta (right) has consistently found life tough when managing away at Anfield

Going to Anfield has become something akin to a hoodoo - and it shows no signs of abating

Arteta surrounded the training pitch with enormous speakers which blared out 'You'll Never Walk Alone' during a training session, in hope the noise would ready his players to tackle the very atmosphere he himself wilted in. It was to no avail.

The Gunners found themselves on the end of a 4-0 drubbing and Arteta on the end of mocking from critics for his alternative methods.

Five years later, Arsenal's away day hoodoo against the Reds has shown no signs of abating.

The north London club's league record against Liverpool away under Arteta reads: six games, three draws, three defeats. Arsenal's most recent league victory there was in September 2012, in which Arteta played in the 2-0 victory.

Their results against Manchester City at the Etihad - their other closest title rivals in recent years - under Arteta are no better either. Seven games have resulted in five defeats and two draws.

In fact, across the 27 Premier League teams Arteta's Arsenal have faced away from home during his seven-year reign, his lowest points-per-game ratios are against Man City (0.29) and Liverpool (0.50).

These matches are more than difficult away trips. They are a test of both Arteta's tactical flexibility and the psycho logical resilience of his team in the face of hostility.

Andoni Iraola's side have appeared to turn a corner in the league after beating the impressive Brighton last weekend. With a cloud of uncertainty hanging over Man City and whether their sanctions for breaching financial rules will be enacted before the season ends, Liverpool may well end up as Arsenal's closest challengers for the title.

Beating Arsenal on Sunday, certainly, would go some way to announcing themselves as true contenders.

Arsenal are champions but they have consistently struggled away against the very best teams

So where have Arteta's Arsenal gone wrong at Anfield and the Etihad Stadium? Well, Arteta's tactical approach has arguably been too cautious in these fixtures for a start.

The 1-0 defeat in August 2025 against Arne Slot's Liverpool smacked of restraint and a concession that a point would be good enough before Dominik Szoboszlai's stunning late free-kick winner.

Arsenal's defensive organisation has long been a major strength under Arteta. He has built his Arsenal from the backline, reinforcing it with excellent back-up options before assessing the forward positions.

Yet, in these high-profile away matches, the pursuit of defensive security can come at the expense of attacking ambition.

There's a big drop in attacking output between when Arsenal face Liverpool at Anfield under Arteta compared with when the Gunners face other league opponents on away turf across the last two seasons.

Possession drops from 56.3 to 43.2 per cent, expected goals from 1.6 to 1.1 and big chances created from 3.1 to 1.8.

The impact of the fervent Anfield atmosphere can't be ignored, either. Ray Parlour understands this better than most, making his Arsenal debut at Anfield in January 1992 aged 18.

The Gunners legend, part of Arsene Wenger's Invincibles side, has a word of advice for the current crop.

'I made my debut there, I know exactly how tough it is to play there. But mentally, you've got to get ready,' Parlour tells Daily Mail Sport.

'For me, the crowd in the first 15 to 20 minutes is always very important at Anfield, because you have to silence them if you can.

Arteta's attack routinely suffers as he seeks defensive solidity in the toughest away games

Arsenal are very strong when they score first but slow starts have proven their Achilles heel

'You've got to start on the front foot, put them under pressure, and I think they can leak goals, Liverpool. To try score that first goal is always important.

'We know defensively Arsenal are a very strong side, so if they go and get that first goal, then they might have a good afternoon there.'

Parlour raises a pertinent point. Arsenal's slow starts at Anfield have left themselves with a mountain to climb. Of the 26 league games Arsenal won last season, they scored first in 24 of those matches. Whereas in the six away matches against Liverpool under Arteta, the Gunners have taken time to getting going.

More shots (from 27 to 30) and an increased xG (from 3.2 to 3.5) were registered in the second period compared to the first half in those games.

Arsenal need to start quicker - and be more clinical, too. At the Emirates, Arteta's men have struck 10 goals against Liverpool, but just six at Anfield despite creating more big chances at Anfield (1.8 per away game vs 1.1 per home game).

Parlour references Arsenal's 3-0 pummelling at Brighton last month as a key example. Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler admitted telling his players to 'win the small battles first' and that's exactly what they did.

'Win the first header, win the first tackle, win the first throw in, win the first corner,' revealed Hurzeler when asked about his pre-match message to his players. The Gunners can use this as a lesson to overcome their bogey team.

'Look, they're champions. They've got to play in all different sort of atmospheres,' explains Parlour.

'There's a lot of experienced players out there, so you know what to expect.

Arteta played in Arsenal's last league win at Anfield - a 2-0 victory 14 years ago against Brendan Rodgers' Liverpool. He will look to end that streak as a manager on Sunday

Former Arsenal midfielder Ray Parlour wants to see a bravery that can help navigate the storm

'It's going to be a tough place to play, but you've just got to go there and play your game. Individuals win their battles, which is very important in football.

'You see Brighton when they turned over Arsenal, they won their battles that day, so you've got to make sure you get one over on the players you're playing against.

Ultimately, if Arteta is to banish the Anfield demons that have lingered for 12 years, Arsenal must arrive with the courage to impose themselves from the first whistle - and the resilience to withstand the inevitable storm. Only then can the Spaniard finally rewrite a story that has haunted him for so long.

#1510. AC Milan: Diego Moreira’s sublime free kick against Inter

What a match from Diego Moreira! While AC Milan was already leading 2-1 against Inter in a spectacular derby, the Belgian international decided to showcase his talent a little more. Despite the Nerazzurri’s strong moment after Alessandro Bastoni’s score was reduced, the Rossoneri won an ideally placed free kick at the edge of the area. Already the author of two assists at the start of the match, Diego Moreira took charge of the shot. And the Belgian didn’t tremble. With a perfectly executed shot, the ball passed just over the wall before ending its journey into the back of the net. A magnificent free kick which allows Ruben Amorim’s men to regain a two-goal lead just before the break (3-1).

An achievement which rewards an exceptional first period from Diego Moreira, involved in all three Milan goals. From the 4th minute, the Belgian opened the scoring to Christian Pulisic, before serving Adrien Rabiot six minutes later on a two-man corner. Despite Inter’s reaction, which occurred in the 21st minute, the AC Milan player gave his team some breathing room thanks to this superb free kick.

#1508. Why Real Madrid and FC Barcelona are no longer recruiting French people

A few years ago, both FC Barcelona and Real Madrid greatly appreciated the French market. Certain players like Aurélien Tchouameni, Eduardo Camavinga or Ferland Mendy are still present in Madrid, while in the 2010s, the Catalan club also enlisted several French players or players playing in Ligue 1. But in recent years, the trend has clearly faded, and if we put aside the market opportunity Ibrahima Konaté or Kylian Mbappé, it is rare to see the two Spanish ogres take an interest in the French market. Of course, there is no doubt that if the possibility of recruiting Michael Olise presented itself, FC Barcelona and especially Real Madrid would jump at it. But it is obvious that in recent years, the two La Liga leaders have turned their backs on French football.

This is not necessarily a talent pool problem, since France continues to produce quality players. First possible explanation: the latest experiences are not really conclusive and therefore do not necessarily invite the two clubs to continue to dig into France. At FC Barcelona, ​​the French and/or Ligue 1 players recently recruited have not been completely satisfactory, on different scales. Malcom, Jean-Clair Todibo, Ousmane Dembélé, Clément Lenglet, Antoine Griezmann and Jules Koundé have some had good moments, but the results are generally bad. At Real Madrid, a similar observation for the players who preceded Karim Benzema or Raphaël Varane. The leaders of the two clubs have therefore perhaps been cooled…

Another explanation, and it is perhaps a little more down to earth than the first: the appearance of new players, and therefore new competitors, on the market. With the appearance of Saudi clubs, and increasingly powerful English clubs, the number of clubs capable of competing with FC Barcelona and Real Madrid has increased considerably. If there could be four or five clubs including Real and Barça on the same player at one time, today there can be around ten. And inevitably this causes colossal inflation in player prices. In 2016, Samuel Umtiti cost FC Barcelona only 25 million euros. Ten years later, there is no doubt that it would have cost at least double.

And it is also valid in the other direction: the power of these new purchasing clubs makes it very complicated to snatch players from them afterwards. FC Barcelona, ​​for example, tried to acquire Eli Junior Kroupi this summer, but Bournemouth demanded a minimum of 100 million euros. A completely prohibitive amount, which Barça cannot or does not want to pay, but which English big names could align themselves with without shaking their chins too much. It must also be said that the recruitment policy of the two clubs has changed: now, we are trying to recruit young players for “correct” sums before they explode and become the stars of tomorrow, a bit like Barça did with Bisiwu or Abdelkarim this summer, and like Real Madrid has been doing for a while too. And players playing in France are already too expensive.

In the case of Barça, we are also obliged to mention this financial crisis which calmed the club’s enthusiasm in the transfer window and which pushed the management to turn, more than was already the case, towards its training center. The decrease in French or Ligue 1 players in the two La Liga giants can also be explained by structural changes. Both, for example, had French managers or advisors internally. Éric Abidal was technical secretary of Barça at the end of the 2010s, and his predecessor, Robert Fernandez, was also an expert in Ligue 1, where he wanted, for example, to enlist Jean Michael Seri. On the Madrid side, Zinédine Zidane, whether as an advisor to Florentino Pérez or as a coach, has also pushed to explore the French market.

Today, Deco and his right-hand man Bojan Krkić, as well as Hansi Flick who also has his say, are not particularly focused on France. At Real Madrid, where Juni Calafat is the main instigator of the transfer windows. Coaches also have decision-making power, although they are not always respected by the hierarchy. The French market is no longer very popular. Calafat is thus more turned towards America, while José Angel Sanchez, general director of the club, is more fond of trying shots in big European clubs. The French are therefore no longer necessarily popular in Spain… until an interesting opportunity presents itself! In the meantime, it’s time for the Clasico!

Roma made history at Old Trafford. Thanks to goals from Soulé and Malen, which came in the first 18 minutes of the match against Manchester United, the Giallorossi set a new record at the English stadium.

Never before had a visiting team managed to score twice so early at Old Trafford in a major European match. Gasperini’s team broke the deadlock in the 11th minute through Soulé, before doubling their lead from the penalty spot seven minutes later through Malen.

This figure applies to all major European competitions played by Manchester United at their home ground, which has never before seen the visiting team score two goals in 17 minutes of play.

#1506. Gasperini analyzes loss to Man United: “It teaches us a lot.”

A terrible late defeat condemned Roma to the Champions League.

Leading the way, the Giallorossi saw Manchester United overturn their lead in the final minutes: first a penalty from Bruno Fernandes, then a brace from Matheus Cunha.

The Brazilian first leveled the scoreline with a mistake from Balerdi, then scored the winner in the 86th minute, capping his wild night with a red card in the 91st.

After the match, Gian Piero Gasperini analyzed the painful defeat to Sky Sport, starting with the episode that changed the match’s momentum: “I think it was a different game than the one against Real Madrid,” the Giallorossi coach explained. “There weren’t such obvious signs of a decline, as there were after the penalty, which gave them a great boost.”

No excuses, however, for the inability to stem the Red Devils’ final assault: “There’s no coincidence in the goals we conceded in the comeback; tonight we didn’t have the strength to defend their attackers. It’s natural that you can struggle against Manchester United in the final 15 minutes if they attack like that.”

“They started to press further forward; we had to play differently, taking advantage of long balls. We weren’t able to keep up with them: we should have resorted to a few more tackles, but instead we suffered their momentum, which was amplified by the penalty and the 2-2 incident.”

On managing the right flank and using Lulli in place of the injured Rensch (with Molina left out): “Molina could have stayed in, yes. Rensch started well, then he got injured and I opted for Lulli. But that’s not the reason for the defeat. I think it was a different match, which taught us more than the one against Real Madrid.” He concluded by focusing on the psychological aspect of dealing with the backlash: “There was a bit of disappointment after seeing victory slip away from you at the front. The team perhaps needs to relieve itself of the pressure of a result at all costs.”
